0.

FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 19 June 1967, after the draft finalized by the Sports Goods Sectional Committee had been approved by the Consumer Products Division Council.
0.2 This standard, dealing with the carrom-draughts, is one of a series of Indian Standards on sports goods and gymnastics equiPment prepared on the recommendations of the Sports Goods Export Promotion Council, New Delhi. Other specifications published so far in the series are given at P 8.

0.3 This standard

contains clauses which call for agreement between the purchaser and the supplier or which permit the purchaser to use The relevant clauses his option for selection to suit his requirements. are 4.1, 6.1 and 8.1. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance \vith IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

4.1 The carrom-draughts shall be manufactured to shape as shown in Fig. 1 or as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. As per the practice existing, these shall have two concentric circles in each face. A minimum of nine carrom-draughts shall be off-white, nine black and the one known as `queen' shall be red. For obtaining off-white colour, if need be, the draughts may be bleached. 4

IS :4143-1967
5. WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH

5.1 Each carrom-draught shall be finished smooth and shall be circular Also, the edge in shape without any protuding edges or uneven face. In case of coloured carrom-draughts, the shall be round and smooth. colour shall not come off by dry or wet rubbing. 6. PACKING 6.1 The earrom-draughts shall be packed in sets, nine white, nine black Each set shall contain extra draughts, at least one white and one red. and one black. The packing shall be as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 7. MARKING 7.1 Each package of a set of carrom-draughts shall carry the manufacturer's name, identification or registered trade-mark. 7.1.1 The packages of carrom-draught the Standard Mark. sets may also be marked with

NOTE - The use of tbe Standard Mark is governed by tbe provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys tbe assurance tbat they have been produced to comply with tbe requirements of tbat standard under a well defined system of inspu3ion, testing and quality control wbicb is devised and supervised by BIS and oprxated by tbe producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details bf conditions under wbicb a license for theuseof theStandard Mark may be granted to manufacturersor producers may be obtained from tbq Bureau of Indian Standards.

all the carrom-draught sets manufactured from the same species of timber shall be grouped together to constitute a lot.

A-3.1 Each carrom-draught set in the sample shall be inspected for material, dimensions, manufacture, workmanship andefinish and tested in accordance with 9.1.1, Any of the draughts in a set failing to meet any one or more of the requirements of this specification shall render the set as a whole to be classified as defective. A-3.2 The lot shall be declared as conforming to the requirements of this specification if the number of defective sets as observed in A-3.1 does not exceed the permissible number of defectives given in co1 3 of Table 1.
